concerns.text: The validation target is the binary presence/absence of a resistance gene (derived from ARIBA). The predictor set includes SNP‑derived features that are called from the same whole‑genome sequence and therefore can directly encode the presence of that gene (e.g., absence of SNPs in the gene region when the gene is missing). Even though the exact target column is removed (mechanism‑blind filter), the remaining SNP features are not independent of the outcome, making the evaluation circular: the model is essentially learning a proxy of the same information it is supposed to predict, guaranteeing high AUC by definition rather than demonstrating a genuine genotype‑to‑phenotype relationship.

The permutation test permutes residuals of a PGLS model that itself is built on the same SNP and gene‑presence data used for prediction. Because the predictors already contain information that deterministically reflects the outcome, the null distribution does not represent a true independence baseline, so the p‑value assessment is not meaningful.
